title: Reconnect and restore a Remote pane by its real program, not a name it mentions
body:
Found by the previous card (commit on main titled "Type the reply note only into an agent program"; read its body). remote::program_agent is now the exact "this program is an agent" predicate, but reconnect (remote::relaunch) and the saved workspace still decide through remote::agent_of, the tab icon's substring scan. So a Remote pane running `vi codex.md` is saved as a Remote agent "codex", and reconnecting it starts a bare `codex resume --last` (or `claude --continue` for a file named claude.txt) instead of rerunning the user's command. That runs a program the human never asked for on their other PC.
The human's standing requirement: proven by driving the real application; reproduce BEFORE the fix, verify AFTER, record both, in the same way as that commit (its card: `foreman kanban list silmcb --json`; reuse its setup: own release builds under target/agent/, config dir target/agent/appdata-s2hp4s restored afterwards, own pipe, test Remote andy@192.168.8.168 key login, a new /tmp directory per run, clean up what you create, never stop a foreman by name, install nothing on the Remote).
Blocked by: Type the reply note only into a real agent program, and two cue follow-ups
Fix:
- Every Remote decision about WHAT TO RUN or WHAT TO TYPE goes through remote::program_agent: relaunch / the RESUME table, whatever the workspace saves and restores as a Remote Session's agent, the disconnect bar's "resume <agent>" wording if it names an agent, and anything else in src/ that calls remote::agent_of (list every call site in the commit body with its verdict). After this, agent_of may remain only for cosmetic uses (tab icon, labels); if nothing cosmetic needs it, remove it.
- A non-agent command that mentions an agent reconnects by rerunning its own command, exactly like any other non-agent Remote command does today.
- A real agent still resumes as today (claude --continue, codex resume --last), including by path and through the npx / wsl wrappers program_agent accepts; a wrapper it does not accept (for example env VAR=1 codex) is NOT an agent for relaunch either: decide and state what it reruns, and keep docs/remote-sessions.md's "a wrapped agent relaunches bare" gotcha true or correct it.
- A workspace saved by an older build that recorded such a pane as an agent must not start the wrong program on restore or reconnect: re-derive from the saved command rather than trusting a saved agent label, or show from the code why no such label is persisted. Test with a fixture of the old shape.
- Table test for relaunch covering the same rows as the typed_route table (vi codex.md, tail -f grok.log, cat claude.txt, a path containing an agent name, bash -c "codex ...", env VAR=1 codex, npx and wsl forms, real agents by name, path and case).
Reproduce live BEFORE (main as it is): open `vi codex.md` on the Remote in a throwaway /tmp directory, stop its ssh child on this PC by PID, `foreman reconnect <terminal>`, snapshot: what started? (Codex may show an update prompt: do NOT answer it, do not type into it, close the pane.) AFTER: the same steps end with vi on codex.md again. Also AFTER, one real agent: a Claude that has done one turn, dropped and reconnected, resumes its conversation (claude --continue) and can post with the new token.
Hard rules as before: nothing assumes foreman on the Remote; a Remote agent's allowed actions are unchanged; no wire change; nothing under cfg(test) spawns a process or socket outside the remote_probe network guard; do not change icons::IconKind::from_argv or the tab icon.
Done when:
- no Remote launch, relaunch, restore, hook, hold or typed-note decision can be triggered by a command that merely mentions an agent (table tests; call-site list in the commit body)
- BEFORE and AFTER observed on the real Remote and recorded in the commit body and a short spec Results entry
- docs/remote-sessions.md and both providers' dispatch skill copies corrected only where now wrong; cite-guard clean; full suite passes
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent; pwsh -File .claude/hooks/cite-guard.ps1 -All
